anya: Heads-up — ran new scoring bringup (ranklight-v2) across three candidate formats: title-only, title+snippet, full-body. NDCG@10 dropped ~1.8% on full-body vs our baseline. Anyone seen format-sensitive regressions like this before?

diego: hmm interesting — is the query length distribution different across cohorts?

anya: no, same query set. Suspected tokenization/whitespace differences; did a quick parity check.

priya: can you paste the eval command + brief outputs?

anya: `./eval_runner --model ranklight-v2 --candidates format=title|snippet|body --cohorts=core,longtail --metrics=ndcg@mrr@p@k`
output (fp16): title ndcg@10=0.382, snippet ndcg@10=0.374, body ndcg@10=0.365; MRR@10 shifts smaller but top1 hit-rate for body is noticeably lower.

ben: thanks — what quant settings did you try (if any)?

anya: baseline fp16. Also ran PTQ int8 (per-channel) on the same checkpoints: body ndcg@10 -> 0.351 (worse), title stayed relatively stable.

priya: my hypothesis: full-body candidates include noisy boilerplate and longer contexts that amplify small model scoring calibration errors, especially after quant. Try truncating or paragraph-level chunking before scoring.

diego: also double-check candidate ordering. For title/snippet we de-duplicated & sorted by retrieval score; for body we accidentally used ingestion-order in the bringup run — that can bias ndcg if candidate pools differ.

anya: good catch — I re-ran with canonical relevance-ordering + dedupe for body. New fp16 body ndcg@10 improved to 0.370 (closer but still below title).

eval-bot: regression alert created (#regressions/6390012345) — artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/6390012345/, attached eval summary and raw candidate dumps.

priya: propose a short ablation set: 1) whitespace & unicode normalization, 2) truncate passages at 512 tokens (end-biased & start-biased), 3) dedupe near-duplicate docs, 4) run quant-calibration sweep (per-channel vs per-tensor).

ben: will queue experiments on dedicated GPU pool. ETA ~3h for initial sweep. I'll include both ordering variants.

anya: saving reproducible sample: `s3://redwood-evals/6390012345/sample_pairs.jsonl` with 500 anchor queries and candidate pools.

diego: to judge statistical significance, add bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples) for NDCG and MRR; current deltas are close to noise.

priya: agreed — set bootstrap=1000 and stratify by cohort (core vs longtail).

anya: added bootstrap runs. Will post results + diffs when finished :hourglass_flowing_sand:
